Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.quote: Small water-soaked spots develop on the upper surface, which develop gray to tan centers with darker borders, and affected foliage eventually turn yellow, then brown, and drop.
Lesions may also develop on stems of infected pepper plants.
Fruits develop small, raised rough spots that do not affect eating quality.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: Initial symptoms include chlorotic spots on the upper leaf surface, which may coalesce and turn necrotic over time.
A white mycelial coating (conidia and conidiophores) appears on the lower leaf surface beneath these spots.
